title: How a Compak® Sporting layout works
summary: Five stations, six traps A to F, a marked rectangle and a menu at each station: how a Compak® Sporting round works and how the squad moves.

body.html: Compak® Sporting is a compact FITASC discipline. It was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991. Unlike Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™, which spreads over natural ground, a Compak field is built to one set plan with fixed sizes.

Compak® Sporting fits on one field. In front of the shooters, a rectangle 35 to 40 m wide and 25 m deep is marked out, with a flagged stake at each corner. The rules require it on each field. When there is no wind, each target must pass over this rectangle at some point of its flight.

The corner stakes are about 50 cm high. The sides of the rectangle are called AB, BC, CD and AD, and AD is the side facing the shooters. The line of stations is parallel to AD and 4 to 8 m behind it, with station 3 opposite its middle.

Five shooting stations, each a 1 m square, stand in a line with 2 to 5 m between their centres. They are numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Each station has a Firing Angle Limiter, a frame of tubes. It limits how far the gun can swing to the sides, up or down, and stops the shooter leaning or stepping forward.

Six traps, A to F from left to right, each carry a panel with their letter. They may be in front, at the sides or behind the shooters; a trap behind the line stands on a tower, at least 4 m above the stations. Each Compak field must have three required flight paths. Two are crossers: one flies across from left to right, the other from right to left, and both pass over sides AB and CD. The third is a going-away target, flying away from the shooters over side BC. The organiser chooses the other flight paths; they stay short so as not to reach the next field.

A round is 25 targets, five at each station. A station's five targets come in one of three mixes: five singles; three singles and one double; or one single and two doubles. On one field all the doubles are of the same kind: either on report (the second target leaves when you fire at the first) or simultaneous (both leave together). The menu, the list of the station's targets in order, is posted at each station. The stations are linked in a chain: the first target of each double is the last target shot at the previous station.
FITASC offers 40 ready-made setting tables (plans of which traps are shot at each station) and advises using them in competitions. How to read a menu card is explained in Reading the target menu.

How a squad of up to six moves along the stations: the shooter on station 1 shoots first, and a sixth shooter waits behind station 1. When the shooter on station 5 has finished, everyone moves one station to the right. The shooter from station 5 goes to wait behind station 1, and the shooter who was waiting steps onto station 1. Change stations with the gun open and unloaded, without disturbing anyone who is still shooting.
You have up to 10 seconds to call for your target after the target of the previous station has been shot. When your turn comes, be ready at once, with cartridges for the whole round.
Some events shoot Compak® Sporting in line instead: every shooter starts on station 1 and finishes on station 5. Ask the organiser which system is used, because the procedure differs.

html.sporting: The gun starts low: the top of the stock stays below the line on the jacket until the target appears.
html.compak: The position is free: the gun may already be at your shoulder (mounted). Each target is still shot with the gun at the shoulder.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Everybody move one to the right. Number five, to the waiting position.
phrases.meaning: The squad rotates; the shooter from station 5 goes behind station 1.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Trap E is the tower — it comes over your head.
phrases.meaning: The target from trap E is thrown from a high tower and passes overhead.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Mind the frame — don't swing past the post.
phrases.meaning: Respect the Firing Angle Limiter; do not swing the gun beyond it.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Move one station to the right.
phrases.meaning: Rotation after the shooter on station 5 has finished.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Gun open when you change stations.
phrases.meaning: Between stations the gun is open and unloaded.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Your double starts with the last target of the previous station.
phrases.meaning: The first target of your double is the same target that was shot last at the station before yours.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: The sixth shooter stands behind station 1.

key_points.html: Rectangle 35–40 m × 25 m; five 1 m stations; six traps A–F.
Compulsory: left-to-right crosser, right-to-left crosser, going-away target.
Round = 25 targets, 5 per station; one kind of double on the whole field.
After station 5: wait behind station 1; everyone moves one station right.
Gun position at the call is free; you have up to 10 seconds to call.

did_you_know.html: Because of the chain of doubles, the referee can show the next shooter the target their double starts with: the last target of the previous station.

quiz.q: How many traps and stations does one Compak® Sporting field have?
quiz.explain: Traps A to F and stations 1 to 5.

quiz.q: The shooter on station 5 has finished his menu. Where does he go?

options.text: To the referee to sign the sheet

quiz.explain: He becomes the waiting shooter behind station 1 while everyone else moves one station to the right.

quiz.q: In Compak® Sporting, how may the gun be held when you call for the target?

options.text: Free: it may already be mounted
Only low, below the line on the vest
Only on the shoulder, muzzles up

quiz.explain: In Compak® Sporting the gun position at the call is free, but you always shoot with the gun mounted. The low gun with a vest line is a Sporting™ rule.
